title: DART impact on Dimorphos
gravity_note: Dimorphos's gravity is about 1/100,000 of Earth's. Escape speed is only about 5 cm/s, slower than a crawling baby, so even standing up too fast could launch you into space.

height.product: DART Dimorphos SPC shape model v004, global 0.487 m (dimorphos_g_0487mm_spc_obj_0000n00000_v004.obj)
height.credit: NASA / JHUAPL / DART Investigation Team (Daly, Barnouin et al.); PDS Small Bodies Node

color.product: Shaded relief rendered from the same shape model
color.credit: Derived from DART Dimorphos shape model v004 (NASA/JHUAPL)

note: Impact site (2022-09-26) from dimorphos_impact_point_model_v004.txt: lat -8.96 +/- 0.45, E long 263.13 +/- 0.47, XYZ (-9.7, -80.4, -12.8) m. This is the PRE-impact surface: DART reshaped Dimorphos, so the real place looks different now. The model resolves 0.49 m on the side DRACO imaged; the hemisphere DRACO never saw is a smooth, low-detail fill. Dimorphos is only about 177 x 174 x 116 m, so a 200 m patch wraps past its edges. "Up" = best-fit plane normal within 50 m; "north" = spin axis projected onto that plane. Colour is shaded relief rendered from the shape model (sun from the north-west), not a photograph; the shape model has no albedo, so brightness only shows slopes. 60% of the patch is beyond the edge of the body (no ground): height there is clamped to the lowest point and colour is black.
